summary: A product shelf fed by a category, a collection, the product context (relevant) or the visitor's history (last_seen).
rules: `dataSource` has no default: a shelf built from a skeleton is empty until you add it. It has exactly three fields, all required: `type`, `slug` and `id`; the storefront fetches by `type` + `slug`, and `section add` refuses a new shelf without `id`. For a category or collection, `id` and `slug` are the cabinet's (yandex-kit-cabinet `list /v1/categories`, `list /v1/collections`; checked on a live store); for `relevant` and `last_seen` both are the type itself (checked on a live store). Pulled shelves often carry no `id`, or one platform-wide value shared by different collections, and some a leftover `slugId`: keep what a pulled shelf stores when you restyle it, and write the three fields for a new one (`presets apply --as-new` does it for relevant and last_seen and asks for the cabinet id otherwise).
One source per shelf per page; the storefront fetches a shelf by `type` + `slug` (7 of 40 home pages in the reference sample repeat a source and show identical rows).
No two same-shaped shelves back to back. The only allowed pair is the bento: a 2-column lead shelf, then an untitled shelf with another column count and `paddingTop: none`.
For grids `count` is a multiple of `columns`.
`layout: feed` does not work with the `relevant` source.
Hide or replace a shelf whose items are all out of stock.
On phones `enableTwoColumnsOnTouch: true` shows 2 cards per row (a carousel shows 2 and a peek); `false` shows one card filling the screen. Keep it true, except for a 2-card statement pair.
A shelf with its own `titleText` hides together with its title when it is empty; a separate heading section above it stays alone on the page.

Card buttons follow the theme card (`productSnippet.buttons.buttonColorInFeaturedProducts`): every preset writes `snippet.enableButton: default`, so all shelves of a page show buttons or none, as on every home page of the reference sample. Force `enabled` or `disabled` only on every shelf of the page at once.

The Split and Yandex points lines (`snippet.yandexSplit`, `snippet.yandexDiscount`) are the store's configuration: presets never write them, a pulled shelf keeps its values and a new one gets the schema default.

`titleAlign` is `default` (as in the theme), `left` or `center`: write `default` unless the preset needs a side; a stored `left` under a centred theme is the most common mixed page (`title-align-mixed`).

presets.name: home-shelf-carousel
presets.use: The primary home shelf (new arrivals or bestsellers): carousel of 4, 12 cards, 2 cards and a peek on phones (about 0.7 of a screen), no card buttons (each adds about 45 px per phone row).
fill: `dataSource`: a real collection or category of the store.

presets.name: home-shelf-grid
presets.use: A static curated grid: one desktop row, 2 by 2 on phones (about 1.2 screens), no buttons. Go to 8 cards only on a short home: that is 4 phone rows.
fill: `dataSource`: another source than the other shelves on the page.

presets.name: shelf-three-large
presets.use: Bigger cards: 3 columns, used as the second shelf to change the rhythm.

presets.name: bento-lead
presets.use: First half of the bento pair: two large statement cards without badges, so the pair reads as one statement. On phones they stack full width, then `bento-follow` shows 2 by 2.
presets.evidence: 2-column shelves in 8 stores, the exact 2 + 4 pair in 5; the 2-card pair stacks on phones in 4 stores and sits 2-up in 1. Hiding the badges is this preset's own choice, not the sample's

presets.name: bento-follow
presets.use: Second half of the bento pair: untitled 4-card row glued under `bento-lead`.
fill: `dataSource`: a different source from the lead shelf.

presets.name: untitled-shelf-under-banner
presets.use: Shelf directly under a banner that names the category.
fill: `dataSource`: the category named on the banner above.

presets.name: gallery-shelf-gapless
presets.use: Edge-to-edge product wall. Only when every packshot shares one backdrop.
presets.evidence: seen in the sample; not counted separately

presets.name: two-column-formats
presets.use: Stores with 1-5 products: all formats as large cards in 2 columns.

presets.name: promo-eligible-grid
presets.use: Promo landing: the products the offer applies to.

presets.name: product-page-similar
presets.use: First shelf under ProductDetails in catalogs of 8 or more products: similar products, titled in the shelf so it hides cleanly when empty. In smaller catalogs keep `relevant` and set the similar products of every card by hand in yandex-kit-cabinet (`similar/add`); a curated collection repeats the product on its own page.
presets.evidence: the relevant source on about 2 in 5 default product pages; empty in small catalogs in the product-page captures
fill: `titleText`, e.g. «Похожие товары»: in the shelf, never in a heading section above it.
`dataSource` of type `relevant`: copy it from an existing similar-products shelf of the store, or write `{"type": "relevant", "slug": "relevant", "id": "relevant"}` (checked on a live store).

presets.name: similar-large-3
presets.use: Image-led brands: similar products as large 3-column cards glued to the product block.

presets.name: recently-viewed
presets.use: Product-page tail and the cart page: the visitor's history. The last shelf before the subscription; never the only shelf and never the first under the product card (a first visitor sees nothing, the next one the product itself). Needs no catalog ids.
presets.evidence: on about 2 in 3 default product pages and 3 in 5 cart pages; the only shelf on about 2 in 5 product pages and the first under the card on about 3 in 10, which is what the tail rule corrects
fill: `dataSource` of type `last_seen`: copy from an existing shelf, or write `{"type": "last_seen", "slug": "last_seen", "id": "last_seen"}`.
